prompt: Convert the Python basics notes file into RemNote flashcards. Read the file at evals/samples/python-basics-notes.md, analyze the programming concepts, data types, syntax, and language features described. Generate a comprehensive set of flashcards choosing the best card type for each concept. Pay attention to bidirectional relationships (like comparing strings vs lists vs tuples) and exam-preparation style distinctions. Output the flashcards to evals/samples/python-basics-notes-flashcards.md.

assertions.name: file_exists_and_non_empty
assertions.description: Output file exists and contains at least 20 flashcards

assertions.name: has_concept_cards
assertions.description: Contains at least 4 Concept cards (::) for key programming concepts like variables, functions, loops, OOP

assertions.name: has_bidirectional_cards
assertions.description: Contains at least 2 Bidirectional Basic cards (<>) comparing related types (e.g., list vs tuple, string vs list)

assertions.name: has_cloze_cards
assertions.description: Contains at least 3 Cloze cards ({{ }}) for syntax facts and key terms

assertions.name: has_multiple_choice
assertions.description: Contains at least 1 Multiple-Choice card (>>A)) for exam-style distinction questions

assertions.name: has_variety_of_types
assertions.description: Uses at least 5 different card types (Concept, Cloze, Bidirectional, Forward Basic, Multiple-Choice)

assertions.name: no_metadata
assertions.description: Contains no HTML comments, metadata, or annotations

assertions.name: covers_data_types
assertions.description: Includes flashcards for: variables, strings, lists, tuples, dictionaries, and comparisons between them
